topic: Discovery stories: oxytocin, the first peptide hormone sequenced and synthesized in a lab (Vincent du Vigneaud, 1953; Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1955 'for the first synthesis of a polypeptide hormone'); Henry Dale found its uterus-contracting effect in 1906 and named it from Greek 'swift birth'; 9 amino acids; lab-made version identical to the natural one; today recommended to help prevent heavy bleeding after birth (FIGO/ICM 2021, based on WHO 2018)

1953 · DISCOVERY STORIES

The first hormone ever built in a lab.

THE CLUE

1906

Henry Dale saw an extract of the pituitary gland make a cat’s uterus contract.

THE NAME

Oxytocin

From Greek: “swift birth.”

A peptide just 9 amino acids long.

1953

Vincent du Vigneaud

1Read its amino acid order.
2Built it from scratch in the lab.

THE TEST

A perfect copy.

The lab-made peptide matched the natural hormone.

1955

Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

Today, it helps prevent heavy bleeding after birth.

Save this for your pharmacology exam.
